newsitem.title: NORWAY: Oslo Total index up with Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: Oslo Total index up with Wall Street.

text.p: Norwegian shares rose marginally on Wednesday with U.S. stocks but trade was slow and some investors seemed to have started Christmas holidays early, dealers said.
The Oslo Total index finished 0.34 percent higher at 923.17 points. "The Norwegian market looks to the United States for impulses," one dealer said.
The bourse fell sharply on Tuesday after overnight losses on Wall Street and stronger than expected U.S. housing starts data.
"We had a bit of a correction today but it is disappointing we could not win back more terrain. It looks like some investors have closed their books on 1996," the dealer said.
Turnover amounted to a healthy 867 million crowns, but it included 241 million crowns stemming from an Aker Maritime sell-off just after the bourse closed.

Industrial group Aker said it sold five percent of its stock in Aker Maritime, leaving it with 75 percent of shares in the offshore company. A statement said 2.83 million shares were sold at 85 crowns per share.

The sell-off was in line with plans for Aker to make sure that at least 30 percent of Aker Maritime shares were controlled by investors other than Aker following the merger between Aker subsidiary Aker Oil and Gas Technology and Maritime Group.
